question: Student 1 would most likely attribute the concentration of failures on the sunlit faces to:

options.A: a larger temperature difference between a panel's center and its edge.
options.B: the slow buildup of stress in the tensile core regardless of temperature.
options.C: stress concentrated at edges chipped during installation.
options.D: faster conversion of the inclusions at higher temperatures.

question: Scientist 2 explains why the layer is thickest at Site A by the action of ocean currents. Which of the following observations, if made, would most weaken this explanation?

options.A: The volcanic glass in the volcanic field 300 km west of Site A contains about 2,000 ppm of nickel, the same as the spherules.
options.B: A spherule layer of the same age, 2.5 cm thick, is found in rock that formed on the bed of a lake 30 km from Site A.
options.C: The limestone beds above and below the spherule layer at Site A were deposited in water more than 200 m deep.
options.D: The spherules at Site C are smaller, on average, than the spherules at Site A.

question: Suppose the students wanted to determine whether the effect of compaction on infiltration rate depends on soil texture. Which of the following changes to Experiment 2 would best allow them to do so?

options.B: Pour 1,000 mL of water rather than 500 mL into each ring.
options.C: Repeat Experiment 2 on sand and clay plots as well as loam.
options.D: Pre-wet the loam plot before each level of compaction.

question: Suppose the students wanted to determine whether the stirring rate affects the dissolution time of a whole tablet. Which of the following changes to the procedure of Experiment 1 would best allow them to do so?

options.A: Hold the stirring rate at 200 rpm and test the tablets at additional temperatures.

options.C: Hold the stirring rate at 200 rpm and test the tablets in HCl of several concentrations.
options.D: Hold the temperature at 20 °C and test the tablets at several different stirring rates.

question: Suppose laboratory tests showed that the virus does not multiply in ticks and becomes undetectable in a tick within 3 days of feeding. This result would most weaken the viewpoint of:

options.A: Scientist 3, because a virus this unstable outside cattle could not survive in well water for long.
options.B: Scientist 1, because midges, like ticks, feed on cattle.
options.C: Scientist 2, because a tick that cannot maintain the virus is unlikely to pass it to a person.
options.D: Scientist 2, because adult ticks are most active in late summer.
